An expert has warned that some UFO encounters feature signs of poltergeist activity, such as telepathy and traits linked to demonic possession

18:47, 09 Sep 2026

Terrifying UFO encounters could be sinister demonic hauntings in disguise, an expert has warned. Diana Pasulka, a professor of religious studies at the University of North Carolina Wilmington, has lifted the lid on creepy parallels between alien sightings and poltergeist activity.

‌

Speaking on an episode of That UFO Podcast, the academic revealed that some close encounters feature telepathy and levitating objects in scenes straight out of a horror film.

‌

Highlighting the uncanny similarities to classic demonic possession, Pasulka said: "You see an entity that seems to know your thoughts and can speak any language and can speak with you without moving their mouth."

‌

Pasulka pointed out that spooky physical disturbances often plague those who claim to have come face-to-face with unidentified flying objects.

She added: "You also see things that are poltergeist-type of activity, you know, things flying and knocks on, you know, walls and scary things like that. So yeah, you do see this with certain UFO experiences."

‌

However, the academic was quick to note that she isn't branding every single saucer sighting as demonic.

She said the chilling comparison was only applicable to specific cases, rather than all UFO reports.

‌

The idea that extraterrestrial visits might actually be dark spiritual forces is not new.

Occultist Marjorie Cameron famously claimed the legendary 1952 Washington UFO wave was a cosmic spiritual reaction to the death of her husband, rocketry pioneer Jack Parsons, a known associate of notorious dark magician Aleister Crowley.

Mid-century evangelist Walter V. Grant Sr released a booklet titled Men in the Flying Saucers Identified: Not a Mystery!, insisting saucer sightings were evil spirits.

‌

American Eastern Orthodox monk Seraphim Rose published Orthodoxy and the Religion of the Future, arguing alien entities were demonic signs designed to draw humanity into the occult.

Renowned British UFO author Gordon Creighton also pushed the theory that mysterious aerial phenomena were supernatural in origin.

Pasulka, whose extensive research into unexplained reports reshaped her own views on faith, noted the encounters feel real to those who experience them, even if science can't explain what's really happening.
